learning_activity_name: Prepare and maintain accounting records and financial statements relating to limited companies (ledger accounts for issue of shares, statements of profit/loss and other comprehensive income, financial position, cash flows and changes in equity excluding debentures, forfeiture and reissue of shares and redemption of preference shares)
sla_name: Preparing financial statements of limited companies
sla_assessment_criteria: Accounting records and financial statements relating to limited companies are correctly prepared.
sla_teaching_aids: Sample of ledger accounts Sample of basic financial statements Sample of share certificate
sla_references: TET(2023), ACCOUNTANCY SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Students prepare ledger accounts for the issue of shares and prepare a limited company's financial statements.
sla_notes_details: When a company issues shares, the ledger records the amount applied for in an Application and Allotment Account, then transfers the nominal value of shares allotted to Share Capital and any excess over nominal value to Share Premium, with unsuccessful applicants refunded; where shares are issued in instalments, separate accounts track amounts due and received at each stage. A limited company prepares a Statement of Profit or Loss and Other Comprehensive Income showing revenue, expenses, tax and any other comprehensive income; a Statement of Financial Position showing assets, liabilities and equity, with equity split into share capital, share premium and reserves including retained earnings; a Statement of Cash Flows classifying cash movements into operating, investing and financing activities; and a Statement of Changes in Equity reconciling the opening and closing balances of each component of equity, showing profit for the year, dividends paid and any new shares issued during the period.
sla_notes_illustrations: A company that issues an additional 200,000 shares of Tsh 1,000 par value at Tsh 1,000 during the year records the proceeds of Tsh 200,000,000 in the Statement of Changes in Equity as an increase in share capital, alongside the profit for the year and dividends paid, to reconcile the opening and closing equity balances.
sla_notes_daily_life: A shareholder reading a company's annual report relies on these statements to see how much profit was made, how the company's cash was used, and how the value of their shareholding has changed over the year.
sla_exercise: What account records amounts received from investors before shares are formally allotted?::The Application and Allotment Account.||Name the four main financial statements a limited company prepares.::The Statement of Profit or Loss and Other Comprehensive Income, the Statement of Financial Position, the Statement of Cash Flows and the Statement of Changes in Equity.||What does the Statement of Changes in Equity show?::How each component of equity, such as share capital, share premium and retained earnings, changed between the opening and closing balances during the period.||Into which three categories are cash flows classified in the Statement of Cash Flows?::Operating activities, investing activities and financing activities.

main_competence_name: Prepare accounting reports
learning_activity_name: Classify costs by behaviour and perform Cost-Volume-Profit (CVP) analysis (compute the break-even quantity and revenue, target quantity and revenue excluding multiple products)
sla_name: Cost classification and Cost-Volume-Profit analysis
sla_assessment_criteria: Classification of costs by behaviour is correctly done and CVP analysis is correctly performed.
sla_teaching_aids: Sample of company targets Sample of revenue sheet
sla_references: TET(2023), ACCOUNTANCY SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Students classify costs by behaviour and perform Cost-Volume-Profit analysis to compute break-even and target sales levels.
sla_notes_details: Costs are classified by behaviour into fixed costs, which remain constant in total regardless of the volume produced within a relevant range, variable costs, which vary in direct proportion to volume, and semi-variable costs, which contain both a fixed and a variable element and must be split before CVP analysis can be applied. Using the contribution margin, selling price less variable cost per unit, the break-even quantity is found by dividing total fixed costs by the contribution per unit, and the break-even revenue is found by multiplying the break-even quantity by the selling price. To find the sales needed to achieve a desired target profit, the target profit is added to fixed costs before dividing by the contribution per unit to get the target quantity, and the target revenue follows by multiplying by the selling price.
sla_notes_illustrations: A product has a selling price of Tsh 4,000 and variable cost of Tsh 2,500, giving contribution of Tsh 1,500 per unit; with fixed costs of Tsh 3,000,000, the break-even quantity is 2,000 units and break-even revenue is Tsh 8,000,000. To earn a target profit of Tsh 1,500,000, the target quantity is 3,000 units, giving target revenue of Tsh 12,000,000.
sla_notes_daily_life: A restaurant owner deciding how many meals must be sold each month to cover rent, salaries and other fixed costs, and how many more must be sold to achieve a desired profit, uses exactly this type of analysis.
sla_exercise: How is the break-even quantity calculated?::By dividing total fixed costs by the contribution per unit.||What is a semi-variable cost?::A cost that contains both a fixed element and a variable element, so it must be split into its two parts before CVP analysis.||How is the quantity needed to achieve a target profit calculated?::By adding the target profit to total fixed costs and dividing the result by the contribution per unit.||What is the contribution-to-sales (profit-volume) ratio used for?::It is used to find break-even revenue directly, by dividing fixed costs by this ratio, without first calculating the break-even quantity.

main_competence_name: Prepare accounting reports
learning_activity_name: Prepare operating budgets (sales, production, purchases, direct labour, overheads and master budget excluding credit sales and credit purchases)
sla_name: Preparing operating budgets
sla_assessment_criteria: Operating budgets are correctly prepared.
sla_teaching_aids: Sample of operating budget
sla_references: TET(2023), ACCOUNTANCY SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Students prepare the functional operating budgets that together form a business's master budget.
sla_notes_details: Budgeting normally begins with the sales budget, which forecasts the quantity and value of sales for the period and is the starting point because most other budgets depend on it; the production budget then converts budgeted sales into the units that must be produced, adjusting for planned changes in finished-goods stock. From the production budget, the materials purchases budget calculates the quantity and cost of materials to buy, again adjusting for changes in raw-material stock, the direct labour budget calculates the labour hours and cost needed to achieve planned production, and the overheads budget estimates indirect production, administration and selling costs. All these functional budgets are finally combined into the master budget, made up of a budgeted income statement and a budgeted statement of financial position.
sla_notes_illustrations: If budgeted sales are 10,000 units, desired closing stock is 1,500 units and opening stock is 1,000 units, the production budget requires 10,500 units to be produced, which then drives the materials and labour budgets.
sla_notes_daily_life: A bakery planning how much flour to buy, how many hours its bakers should work and how much profit it expects next quarter prepares exactly this sequence of budgets before the season begins.
sla_exercise: Why does budgeting normally start with the sales budget?::Because the level of expected sales determines the level of production and resources needed, so most other budgets are built from it.||How is the production budget calculated from the sales budget?::By adding the desired closing stock of finished goods to budgeted sales and subtracting the opening stock of finished goods.||What two statements make up the master budget?::The budgeted income statement and the budgeted statement of financial position.||What does the materials purchases budget calculate?::The quantity and cost of raw materials that must be bought, based on the production budget and planned changes in raw-material stock.

main_competence_name: Demonstrate mastery of professional ethics in Accountancy
specific_competence_name: Demonstrate an understanding of the principles and practice of professional ethics in Accountancy
learning_activity_name: Describe the professional code of ethics for Accountants (integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour)
sla_name: Professional code of ethics for accountants
sla_assessment_criteria: Professional code of ethics for accountants is well described.
sla_teaching_aids: NBAA|IFAC Guidelines
sla_references: TET(2023), ACCOUNTANCY SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Students describe the fundamental principles of professional ethics that accountants in Tanzania are expected to observe.
sla_notes_details: Professional accountants, including those registered with the National Board of Accountants and Auditors (NBAA) and guided by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) code, are expected to observe five fundamental ethical principles. Integrity requires an accountant to be straightforward and honest in all professional relationships. Objectivity requires that professional judgement is not compromised by bias, conflict of interest or undue influence from others. Professional competence and due care require an accountant to maintain the knowledge and skill needed to provide a competent service and to act diligently in accordance with applicable standards. Confidentiality requires an accountant to respect and protect the privacy of information acquired through professional relationships and not disclose it without proper authority, unless there is a legal or professional right or duty to do so. Professional behaviour requires compliance with relevant laws and regulations and avoiding any conduct that discredits the profession.
sla_notes_illustrations: An accountant who discovers that a client is understating income to reduce tax must not help conceal it, which relates to integrity, must not let personal friendship with the client cloud professional judgement, which relates to objectivity, and must not disclose the client's confidential financial details to unrelated third parties without authority, which relates to confidentiality.
sla_notes_daily_life: Whenever people trust an accountant with a business's financial records, tax returns or an audit, that trust depends on the accountant genuinely following these ethical principles rather than favouring the client, an employer or personal gain.
sla_exercise: Name the five fundamental principles of professional ethics for accountants.::Integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality, and professional behaviour.||What does the principle of objectivity require of an accountant?::That professional or business judgement is not compromised by bias, conflict of interest or the undue influence of others.||Under the principle of confidentiality, when may an accountant disclose a client's information?::Only where there is proper authority to do so, or a legal or professional right or duty to disclose it.||Which body registers and regulates professional accountants in Tanzania?::The National Board of Accountants and Auditors (NBAA).

main_competence_name: Use ICT to analyse financial statements
specific_competence_name: Use computer programmes in financial analysis
learning_activity_name: Use accounting packages to analyse financial statements (profitability, liquidity, efficiency and financial leverage ratios excluding market- based ratios)
sla_name: Using accounting software to analyse financial statements
sla_assessment_criteria: Various financial ratios are correctly computed and interpreted.
sla_teaching_aids: Samples of financial statements Accounting software
sla_references: TET(2023), ACCOUNTANCY SYLLABUS FOR ADVANCED SECONDARY EDUCATION FORM V-VI, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Students use accounting packages and computer applications to compute and interpret financial ratios from a set of financial statements.
sla_notes_details: Modern accounting packages and spreadsheet software allow financial statement figures to be entered once and used to automatically compute ratios such as gross profit margin, net profit margin, the current ratio, the quick ratio, inventory turnover, debtors' collection period and gearing ratios, saving time and reducing the risk of manual calculation errors. To use such tools effectively, figures from the Statement of Profit or Loss and the Statement of Financial Position are entered accurately, formulas are built or selected to compute each ratio, and the results for one period can be compared with prior periods or with other businesses using charts generated by the software. Interpreting the output still requires accounting knowledge: a high current ratio computed by software may look favourable but still requires the accountant to judge whether the underlying current assets, such as inventory, are truly liquid.
sla_notes_illustrations: A student enters a company's revenue, cost of sales, current assets and current liabilities into a spreadsheet with formulas for gross profit margin and the current ratio; the spreadsheet instantly recalculates both ratios and displays a chart comparing them with the previous year's figures once new numbers are typed in.
sla_notes_daily_life: A small business owner using accounting software such as a computerised bookkeeping package can quickly see whether the business is more or less liquid and profitable than last month, without doing all the ratio calculations by hand.
sla_exercise: Give one advantage of using accounting software to compute financial ratios rather than calculating them manually.::It saves time and reduces the risk of calculation errors compared with manual computation.||Name three categories of ratios that can be computed from a company's financial statements using accounting software.::Profitability ratios, liquidity ratios and efficiency (or gearing) ratios, for example gross profit margin, the current ratio and inventory turnover.||Why is accounting knowledge still needed even when software computes the ratios automatically?::Because the software only performs the calculation; interpreting what the resulting ratios mean for the business still requires accounting judgement.||What two financial statements provide the figures needed to compute most financial ratios?::The Statement of Profit or Loss (income statement) and the Statement of Financial Position.
